evidence.section: 2.1 As-Cast NiAlCrFeMo High-Entropy Alloy
evidence.quote: Using a non-consumable vacuum arc furnace, bulk Ni, Al, Cr, Fe, and Mo metals with a purity of no less than 99.9% were successfully melted to prepare NiAlCrFeMo high-entropy alloy ingots.

evidence.section: 2.1 As-Cast NiAlCrFeMo High-Entropy Alloy
evidence.quote: To ensure chemical homogeneity, the alloy ingots were melted at least four times on both sides and subsequently suction-cast into a water-cooled copper mold.

evidence.section: 2.1 As-Cast NiAlCrFeMo High-Entropy Alloy
evidence.quote: Eight alloy sheets with dimensions of 72 × 50 × 13 mm were cut from the alloy ingot using a wire-cutting device

evidence.section: 2.2 Hot-Rolling and Mechanical Properties Test Experiment
evidence.quote: The rolling temperature was precisely controlled by heating the samples to the target temperature (1000, 1050, and 1100 °C) at a rate of 10 °C/min, holding them at the temperature for 10 minutes to ensure uniformity, and then immediately transferring them to the rolling mill.

evidence.section: 2.2 Hot-Rolling and Mechanical Properties Test Experiment
evidence.quote: The rolled sheets were labeled as HR1000, HR5, HR1100, HR300, HR900, HR10, HR15, and HR20, corresponding to the following conditions: 1000 °C-600 r/min-5% reduction, 1050 °C-600 r/min-5% reduction, 1100 °C-600 r/min-5% reduction, 1050 °C-300 r/min-5% reduction, 1050 °C-900 r/min-5% reduction, 1050 °C-600 r/min-10% reduction, 1050 °C-600 r/min-15% reduction, and 1050 °C-600 r/min-20% reduction.

evidence.section: 3.2.1 Influence of Reduction Amounts on Phases
evidence.quote: as the reduction percentage increases from 5 to 20%, the percentage of the FCC structure first decreases and then increases, dropping from 66 to 53.9%, and then rising to 60.1%

evidence.section: 3.2.1 Influence of Reduction Amounts on Phases
evidence.quote: the percentage of the BCC structure first increases and then decreases, rising from 34 to 46.1%, and then falling to 39.9%
